name: Elegance and Insight Rubric v2
description: Two-step scoring: (1) rate each of 4 sub-criteria H/M/L, (2) count H scores and map to final score. Includes worked examples at each score level.

criteria.name: SC-A: Conceptual Core
criteria.description: Names a single structural or conceptual reason why the result holds.
checks: Does the answer name a key structural fact (symmetry, contradiction, invariant, pigeonhole)?
Or does it bury the core reason in algebra?
Or merely work through an algorithm without naming the mechanism?

criteria.name: SC-B: Economy of Means
criteria.description: Delivers the key idea compactly without unnecessary scaffolding.
checks: Could the core idea be stated in 1-3 sentences?
Are extra steps clearly subordinate illustration?
Or are there long chains of algebraic manipulation?

criteria.name: SC-C: Explanatory Force (WHY not HOW)
criteria.description: Reveals the mechanism; student understands WHY not just HOW.
checks: After reading, does a student understand WHY the result holds?
Does the answer transmit a transferable principle?
Or is it purely procedural with only local step-by-step justifications?

criteria.name: SC-D: Avoidance of Mechanical Grinding
criteria.description: Deliberately avoids brute-force when a principled shortcut exists.
checks: Does it avoid or critique exhaustive case-bashing?
Does it take the principled path over computer assistance?
Or does it use Wolfram Alpha / plug-and-grind when a conceptual route is available?

aggregation: Count H scores: 4H=1.0, 3H=0.75, 2H=0.5, 1H=0.25, 0H=0.0. SC-A=L caps score at 0.25.

scores.1.0: ALL four sub-criteria HIGH: e.g. lower-triangular eigenvalue observation
scores.0.75: THREE sub-criteria HIGH: clear insight but some algebraic bookkeeping
scores.0.5: TWO sub-criteria HIGH: clever pivot but rest is algebraic expansion
scores.0.25: ONE sub-criterion HIGH: correct and organized but purely procedural (e.g. I-E counting)
scores.0.0: NONE: bare link/reference, one-liner stating answer only, or wall of computation

worked_examples.summary: Bare link to textbook, no explanation
Correct I-E counting walkthrough, pedagogical but mechanical
Clever substitution u=x-pi/3 but rest is algebraic expansion
Rationalizing conjugate + triangle inequality, clear insight with some bookkeeping
Lower-triangular structure: eigenvalues = diagonal entries, nothing to calculate
